hook: A brief mate encounter leaves male worms in a lasting search state, held in place by a neuropeptide.
hook_turn: held in place by a neuropeptide.
summary: After brief contact with a mate, male C. elegans keep searching locally, and optogenetic activation of ray sensory neurons reproduces this. Glutamate drives the initial network response, while the neuropeptide NLP-13 from LUA interneurons sustains activity and the behavior. This is a worm circuit, so how far it applies to other animals is unclear.
title: A Glutamate-Neuropeptide Circuit Converts Transient Mate Contact into a Persistent Local Search State in Caenorhabditis elegans Males
